page: Microsoft Azure L4s is an x86_64 architecture server belonging to the LS family, virtualized via Microsoft Hyper-V. It features 4 dedicated physical cores powered by an Intel Xeon 8370C processor running at 2.8 GHz, with 1.0 thread per core. The hardware configuration includes 32.0 GB of system memory, providing a resource density of 8.0 GB per core. For local storage, the instance is equipped with 694 GB of Premium Storage capable capacity, while it does not include any GPU accelerators.

Performance benchmarks indicate a split profile. The server demonstrates average capabilities in memory bandwidth for large blocks, with read-only speeds at 50.82 GB/sec and write speeds at 33.22 GB/sec. It also achieves average results in Redis SET operations at 6.03 million operations per second and static web serving throughput at 6.22 GB/sec. However, compute-heavy tasks show limitations, with stress-ng single-core performance falling into the bottom 10% and multi-core CPU performance categorized in the bottom 25%. Similarly, Passmark database operations and Geekbench multi-core scores remain in the bottom 25%.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the L4s offers a high memory-to-vCPU ratio and substantial local storage capacity, making it a viable option for workloads requiring moderate memory density without demanding high-performance compute. The tradeoff lies in its weaker CPU processing power and lower memory bandwidth for small blocks. This server is best suited for workloads such as static web serving, lightweight Redis caching, and basic database operations that benefit from local storage and 32.0 GB of RAM but do not require intensive multi-threaded CPU calculations.
